summary: The bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to impose a 180-day deadline (with automatic approval after 210 days if the state already runs another injection well program) on EPA decisions approving or disapproving state applications for primary enforcement authority over Class VI carbon-dioxide injection wells, while requiring prompt completeness reviews, detailed delay notices, pre-application coordination, and transfer of pending permits.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes use of existing IIJA funds for a required EPA resource report and requires EPA to assess any additional funding needs for implementation. This is a minor procedural reference to existing appropriations with no new spending authorization or reduction, so the bill has no meaningful bearing on government spending levels.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare delivery, insurance, or public health programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, visas, or border policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to reproductive health or abortion access.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.

The bill amends the Safe Drinking Water Act to expedite state primacy applications for Class VI wells (used for CO2 geologic sequestration under the IIJA). It imposes strict EPA timelines, automatic approval mechanisms, and limits on conditioning approvals. While it does not alter substantive environmental standards, the procedural changes facilitate faster state assumption of regulatory authority over CCS projects, which has a tangential effect of reducing potential federal regulatory delays.
